I ran the pinned govulncheck (v1.8.0) locally with go1.27.1, before and after this change:

title: `gh` skill description does not tell agents when to use it, so it is skipped for tasks it covers

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: needs to be reviewed

body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

The official `gh` skill (`skills/gh/SKILL.md`) has this description:

> Patterns for invoking the GitHub CLI (gh) from agents. Covers structured output, pagination, repo targeting, search vs list, gh api fallback.

Agents decide whether to load a skill from its description alone. This one has two gaps:

1. It has no "use when" clause, so it says what the skill contains but not which tasks should trigger it.
2. It lists only topics agents already roughly know (`--json`, pagination, `gh api`). It does not mention what the skill uniquely teaches: features newer than most models' training data, such as `--attach`, `gh discussion`, `gh repo read-file` / `read-dir`, and issue types, sub-issues and blocked-by relationships.

Because of this, the skill is skipped for exactly the tasks where it adds the most value. An agent that doesn't know `gh` can do something will never pick `gh` for the task, and so never reaches the skill.

Observed example: in a Claude Code session with the `gh` skill installed, I asked the agent to attach a file to a pull request description. It did not load the skill. It tried to do it through a browser instead, failed (including at login), and eventually gave up. It completed the task with `gh pr edit --attach` only after I told it to use the `gh` skill.

I have since worked around this with a personal `CLAUDE.md` instruction to load the skill before any GitHub task, but other users of the skill won't have that.

### Proposed solution

Rewrite the `description` in `skills/gh/SKILL.md` so that it:

- starts with the tasks that should trigger it ("Use for any GitHub task done through `gh`..."), and
- names the newer capabilities the skill documents, so that agents load it for tasks they wrongly assume `gh` can't do.

For example:

> Use for any GitHub task done through `gh`: issues, PRs, search, `gh api`, attaching images or videos to issues, PRs and comments, discussions, reading repo files without cloning, and issue types, sub-issues and blocked-by links. Covers features newer than most agents' training data, plus structured output, pagination and repo targeting.

This would make the skill trigger more reliably without changing its body. It also matters more if #14615 ships, since packaging the skill as a plugin puts it in front of more users who have no local workaround.

Possible acceptance criteria:

- The description contains an explicit "use when" trigger covering GitHub tasks in general.
- The description names the skill's capabilities that are likely to be missing from a model's training data (at least `--attach`).
- The description stays within agent skill frontmatter limits.

### Additional context

`gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)`; skill installed from `skills/gh` at `v2.101.0`, and the description is unchanged on `trunk`.

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

On every invocation, `gh` registers a cobra command for each installed extension. While registering, it decides whether to record telemetry for that extension: only official GitHub-owned extensions (`github/gh-aw`, `github/gh-stack`, `cli/gh-webhook`) are allowed to. That check called `ext.Owner()` for every installed extension before comparing names.

For extensions installed with `gh extension install` from a repository without release binaries (script extensions), the extension is a git clone, and `Owner()` resolves the owner by running `git config remote.origin.url`. That meant one `git` process per script extension on every `gh` command, including `gh --version` and `gh help`.

This change makes `extensions.IsOfficial` take the extension and resolve the owner only after the name matches an official extension. Third-party extensions, which are nearly all of them, never trigger the owner lookup.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I built `gh` from `trunk` and from this branch, then set up an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` containing 5 git-cloned script extensions (`gh-one` to `gh-five`, each with an `origin` remote of `https://github.com/someone/gh-<name>.git`). `gh extension list` showed all five as `someone/gh-*`.

I then ran hyperfine on `gh --version` (macOS, Apple M4 Max):

```
$ hyperfine -N --warmup 10 --runs 100 -n "before (trunk)" "gh-before --version" -n "after (this PR)" "gh-after --version"
Benchmark 1: before (trunk)
  Time (mean ± σ):      46.3 ms ±   3.5 ms    [User: 27.0 ms, System: 18.0 ms]
  Range (min … max):    42.3 ms …  63.4 ms    100 runs

Benchmark 2: after (this PR)
  Time (mean ± σ):      20.6 ms ±   1.4 ms    [User: 17.6 ms, System: 6.3 ms]
  Range (min … max):    18.7 ms …  27.9 ms    100 runs

Summary
  after (this PR) ran
    2.24 ± 0.23 times faster than before (trunk)
```

That is about 5 ms saved per script extension per invocation. With no extensions installed I measured about 22 ms for both builds, so this change returns startup to roughly the no-extension baseline.

To check that telemetry gating is unchanged, I added a git-cloned `gh-stack` extension with an `origin` of `https://github.com/github/gh-stack.git` and ran both builds with `GH_TELEMETRY=log`:

- `gh stack` logged a `command_invocation` event with `"command": "gh stack"` on both builds.
- `gh one` (a third-party extension) logged no command event on either build.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- `IsOfficial` now takes an `extensions.Extension` instead of `(name, owner string)`. It had a single caller, and passing the extension lets the function decide whether the owner is needed, so callers can't accidentally resolve it eagerly again.
- The owner is looked up at most once, because official extension names are unique in the registry.
- Binary extensions (with a `manifest.yml`) and local extensions were cheap before (a small file read, or nothing), so users with only those see no measurable change. The gain is specific to git-installed script extensions and grows with how many are installed.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with `pkg/extensions/official.go`. The existing `TestIsOfficial` cases are kept unchanged in behavior and now use `ExtensionMock`. `TestIsOfficial_DoesNotResolveOwnerForUnofficialNames` asserts that `Owner()` is not called for a non-official name.

title: Package the official `gh` skill as a Claude Code plugin and emit install hints

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: a request to improve CLI

labels.name: core
labels.description: This issue is not accepting PRs from outside contributors

body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

GitHub CLI provides an official Agent Skill for teaching coding agents how to use `gh`, but Claude Code users must currently discover and install it themselves.

Claude Code supports [plugin hints](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-hints), through which a CLI can recommend an official plugin by writing a structured `<claude-code-hint />` line to stderr. Claude Code strips the line from command output and, when the session is eligible, offers the user a one-time installation prompt.

To use this mechanism, the existing `gh` skill needs to be packaged as a Claude Code plugin, published through an eligible official marketplace, and recommended when Claude Code invokes `gh`.

Anthropic's official marketplace already contains [`github@claude-plugins-official`](https://claude.com/marketplace/plugins/github), which packages the official GitHub MCP server. That plugin provides GitHub API tools; it does not package the `cli/cli`-maintained Agent Skill or teach Claude Code to use the installed `gh` command. The proposed `gh` plugin is distinct from the existing GitHub MCP plugin: it packages the maintained skill for using the local `gh` executable and does not modify or replace the MCP integration.

### Proposed solution

Package the existing official `gh` skill as a Claude Code plugin and publish it through an eligible official marketplace under an agreed permanent identifier.

#### Plugin source and maintenance

Keep `cli/cli` as the source of truth rather than maintaining a second copy of the skill in the marketplace repository. Anthropic's official marketplace supports manifestless skill bundles sourced from another repository, so the entry could use a reviewed, pinned `cli/cli` commit:

```json
{
  "name": "gh",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/cli/cli.git",
    "path": "skills",
    "ref": "trunk",
    "sha": "<reviewed-commit-sha>"
  },
  "strict": false,
  "skills": ["./gh-skill"]
}
```

Under this model:

- `cli/cli` owns the skill source, tests, and compatibility.
- The official marketplace pins a reviewed `cli/cli` commit rather than copying the skill.
- Updating the plugin advances that pin through a marketplace pull request, potentially using automation.
- Anthropic retains review and publication control for the official catalog.
- A skill change is not considered published to plugin users until the marketplace entry points to a reviewed commit containing it.
- Existing installations receive published changes through the official marketplace's default auto-update behavior.

#### Plugin hint emission

When `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty, every `gh` process invocation should write exactly one valid hint on its own stderr line:

```text
<claude-code-hint v="1" type="plugin" value="<registered-plugin>@<official-marketplace>" />
```

Use `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` rather than `CLAUDECODE` so commands manually entered in a Claude Code IDE-integrated terminal do not produce a raw hint. This establishes Claude Code 2.1.172 as the minimum version for automatic discovery.

Child-process terminal state and outer-session eligibility are separate concerns. `gh` should not inspect whether its standard streams are attached to a TTY or attempt to infer whether Claude Code can show a prompt. Claude Code decides whether to display the recommendation from the eligibility of the outer session.

The emitter should:

- Run for every invocation, including help commands, successful commands, and commands that fail.
- Ignore whether stdin, stdout, or stderr is attached to a TTY; child-process terminal state is not a protocol signal.
- Emit exactly once per `gh` process.
- Preserve the command's existing stdout, stderr, and exit status.
- Remain stateless: `gh` should not inspect whether the plugin is installed or remember whether the user rejected it.
- Emit nothing when `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is unset or empty.

Claude Code remains responsible for stripping the tag, checking marketplace and policy eligibility, installing the plugin, and suppressing repeat prompts. `gh` continues emitting after the user rejects or installs the plugin; Claude Code silently ignores subsequent hints.

#### Acceptance criteria: install the official plugin

```gherkin
Feature: Install the official gh plugin

  Scenario: Install the plugin from its recommendation
    Given the official `gh` plugin is listed in an eligible official marketplace
    And the plugin is not installed at user scope
    And Claude Code displays the official `gh` plugin recommendation
    When the user chooses "Yes, install"
    Then Claude Code installs the registered official `gh` plugin at user scope

  Scenario: Use the maintained skill in a subsequent session
    Given the official `gh` plugin is installed at user scope
    When the user starts a subsequent Claude Code session
    Then the maintained `gh` skill is available in that session
```

#### Acceptance criteria: emit and process the recommendation

```gherkin
Feature: Discover the official gh plugin from gh

  Scenario: Emit the plugin hint for a successful command
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    And the official `gh` plugin has a registered identifier in an eligible official marketplace
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line containing the registered plugin identifier to stderr
    And the hint occupies its own line
    And the standard version output is written to stdout
    And the command exits successfully

  Scenario: Emit the plugin hint for a help command
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh help`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And the standard help output is written to stdout
    And the command exits successfully

  Scenario: Emit the plugin hint for a failing command
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh this-command-does-not-exist`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And the standard unknown-command error is written to stderr
    And the command exits unsuccessfully

  Scenario Outline: Emit independently of standard stream terminal state
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    And stdin is <terminal state>
    And stdout is <terminal state>
    And stderr is <terminal state>
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And the standard version output is written to stdout
    And the command exits successfully

    Examples:
      | terminal state        |
      | attached to a TTY     |
      | not attached to a TTY |

  Scenario: Run gh without the child-session variable
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is not set
    When the user runs `gh version`
    Then stderr is empty
    And the standard version output is written to stdout
    And the command exits successfully

  Scenario: Run gh with an empty child-session variable
    Given `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is empty
    When the user runs `gh version`
    Then stderr is empty
    And the standard version output is written to stdout
    And the command exits successfully

  Scenario: Show the recommendation in an eligible outer session
    Given the outer Claude Code session is local
    And the outer Claude Code session is interactive
    And the outer Claude Code session is attended
    And analytics are enabled
    And plugin installation hints are enabled
    And the official `gh` plugin is not installed
    And policy permits the official `gh` plugin
    And `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then Claude Code displays the "Plugin recommendation" dialog
    And the dialog names the official `gh` plugin
    And the dialog names its official marketplace

  Scenario: Continue normally in a non-interactive outer session
    Given the outer Claude Code session is non-interactive
    And `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And Claude Code displays the standard command result
    And the plugin hint is not shown in the command output
    And the "Plugin recommendation" dialog is not displayed

  Scenario: Continue normally after the user rejects the recommendation
    Given the user previously chose "No" for the official `gh` plugin recommendation
    And `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And Claude Code displays the standard command result
    And the plugin hint is not shown in the command output
    And the "Plugin recommendation" dialog is not displayed

  Scenario: Continue normally when the plugin is already installed
    Given the official `gh` plugin is installed
    And `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION` is non-empty
    When Claude Code invokes `gh version`
    Then `gh` writes exactly one valid `claude-code-hint` line to stderr
    And Claude Code displays the standard command result
    And the plugin hint is not shown in the command output

- **gh checks for a match before it saves.** Every save adds a version to the edit history, even when nothing changed.   ```go
  v, err := shared.FindVersion(current, opts.RestoreVersion)
  if err != nil {
  	// A version that isn't in the edit history fails here, before anything is saved
  	return err
  }
  // The current version, or an older one with the same name and content
  if v == nil || (v.Name == current.Name && v.Body == current.Body) {
  	shared.PrintUnchanged(opts.IO, result, message, reason)
  	return nil
  }
  // Otherwise, the version's name and content are saved as a new version
  updated, err := c.Update(repo, opts.IssueNumber, opts.ArtifactNumber, &v.Name, &v.Body)
  ```

- **A restore makes no extra request.** `edit` already gets the artifact before it saves, and that response includes the edit history. [`FindVersion`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5f85ec828f6d2fe28d81ba71a61b8a2181edfb6a/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/shared/shared.go#L66-L82) is the same lookup `view --version` and `download --version` use.
- **The version's name and content are sent as the API returned them.** gh doesn't check them again, so the server checks them like any other edit, including a link's URL.
- **A restore with nothing to do gets a new result line.** In a terminal, `PrintSkip`'s line goes to stdout with the successes. This one is a warning on stderr, so [`PrintUnchanged`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5f85ec828f6d2fe28d81ba71a61b8a2181edfb6a/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/shared/results.go#L55-L67) prints it. Piped, it's the same `skipped` line. No other command's output changes.
- **The `--restore-version` usage error is checked first.** So `--restore-version 5 --body x --body-file y` names `--restore-version`, not the `--body` and `--body-file` conflict. An empty `--body-file ''` names no file, as elsewhere in `edit`, so it doesn't conflict.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

Start with [`restoreVersion`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5f85ec828f6d2fe28d81ba71a61b8a2181edfb6a/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/edit/edit.go#L235-L263), then the [flag checks](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5f85ec828f6d2fe28d81ba71a61b8a2181edfb6a/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/edit/edit.go#L100-L118) in `NewCmdEdit`. [`TestEditRun`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/5f85ec828f6d2fe28d81ba71a61b8a2181edfb6a/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/edit/edit_test.go#L389-L1642) has rows the recording can't show: failed saves, a link's earlier version, a name and content sent exactly as returned, and a type gh doesn't know.

These messages aren't in #14526:

- `X Failed to restore artifact 9: Not Found`, for an artifact that doesn't exist.
- `X Failed to restore artifact 2: <reason>`, for a save the server refuses, with the server's message as the reason.

Piped, both are `failed` lines.

Related issues:

- #14526 is the `edit` design, with a screen for each `--restore-version` scenario.

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

Issue artifacts are Markdown documents and links attached to an issue. The previous pull requests added `gh issue artifact` with six commands: `list`, `view`, `create`, `edit`, `delete` and `download`.

The installable `gh` agent skill doesn't describe them. Agents using the skill would miss how commands address an artifact, what each command takes, the flag combinations each one refuses and the result lines that scripts read. Its `--attach` section also lists only the six earlier commands, though `gh issue artifact create` and `edit` take `--attach` too.

This adds an [**Issue artifacts** section](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/92561b6aad6988bf6e98d5ffe2bdf1425b9c74c1/skills/gh/SKILL.md#issue-artifacts-gh-issue-artifact) to the skill, after **Discussions** and in the same style. For each command, it gives a usage line and what an agent needs to call it correctly. Then it gives the rules the commands share:

- The issue argument is a number or an issue URL. Pull requests and GitHub Enterprise Server are refused.
- `--json` is on `list` and `view` only.
- When piped, `create`, `edit`, `delete` and `download` print one line per artifact with five tab-separated columns. Any failure exits 1.
- `delete` needs `--yes` without a terminal, and standard input is read only through `--body-file -`.
- `download` names files `<number>-<name>`, and saves links as `.url` files that `create` and `edit` read back.

It also adds the two commands to [**Attaching images and videos**](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/92561b6aad6988bf6e98d5ffe2bdf1425b9c74c1/skills/gh/SKILL.md#attaching-images-and-videos), with what differs for them. `--attach` works only on documents. With several documents, `create` refuses a file that no document references. `edit` with only `--attach` appends to the current content.

The API doesn't return artifact URLs yet, as discussed in #14529, so `view` keeps the first design: the footer links to the issue, and `--web` refuses a document with "artifact 2 is not a link; --web only opens link artifacts". A later pull request in this stack will add URLs.
- **`--version` picks from the versions the API returned.** The API returns them newest first, including the current one. [`findVersion`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2a4a25dadf541059b5a5c4cbda9e063a63d3b619/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/view/view.go#L163-L178) looks the number up in that list:

  ```go
  i := slices.IndexFunc(a.Versions, func(v client.Version) bool { return v.Version == number })
  switch {
  case i < 0:
  	// Not among the versions the API returned
  	return nil, fmt.Errorf("version %d not found for artifact %d", number, a.Number)
  case i == 0:
  	// The newest version is the current one, so show the default view
  	return nil, nil
  }
  return &a.Versions[i], nil
  ```

  `--version` can't be combined with `--json`, since `--json versions` has every version, or with `--web`.
- **Types gh doesn't know are refused.** As discussed in #14529, a new artifact type needs a gh update, since it can need handling gh doesn't have. Until then, `view` fails with `artifact 7 has type "bad-type", which this version of gh doesn't support; upgrade gh`, with `--json` too. `list` still lists them.
- **`--web` shows the whole URL.** `gh issue view --web` shortens its message with `text.DisplayURL`, which drops the port, query and fragment. A link can point anywhere, so `view` shows it whole. The [shared check](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2a4a25dadf541059b5a5c4cbda9e063a63d3b619/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/shared/shared.go#L95-L112) accepts only an absolute http or https URL with a host, in printable ASCII with no spaces.

- **The edit history is a table without a header.** The bold "Edit history" heading stands in for column headers, so it uses the table printer's `NoHeader`, like `gh codespace view`. "Current" is bold cyan, like "Newest comment" in `gh issue view`.
- **Null values.** A null user shows as `ghost` when its time exists, and a null time leaves out its part of the line. Piped output prints empty fields, and `--json` keeps null.

### Key points

<!--

- **The header counts only what's shown.** #14523 shows "Showing 3 of 3 artifacts", which needs a total count. The API returns none, so the header says "Showing 3 artifacts on monalisa/monas-cafe#142". With `--type`, it ends with "that match your search", as in #14523.
- **No `url` field yet.** List responses don't include an artifact URL today, so `url` isn't among the `--json` fields. A later pull request in this stack will add it.
- **Both document types are fetched and merged.** In #14523, `--type generic` also lists plans, and `--type plan` also lists generic artifacts. Each request filters on one type on the server, so either value asks for both types, up to the limit, then merges them in [`listArtifacts`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/160715502db6aa37ce280d0c3b960f0042f42d31/pkg/cmd/issue/artifact/list/list.go#L133-L158):

  ```go
  // Either document type asks for both, each up to the limit
  for _, documentType := range []string{client.TypeGeneric, client.TypePlan} {
  	documents, err := c.List(repo, issueNumber, documentType, limit)
  	...
  	artifacts = append(artifacts, documents...)
  }

  // Then number order, cut to the limit
  slices.SortStableFunc(artifacts, func(a, b client.Artifact) int {
  	return cmp.Compare(a.Number, b.Number)
  })
  ```

  Rows keep their stored type, so a plan still shows `plan`.
- **Every page has the same size.** Each request asks for the smaller of `--limit` and 100, and pages continue until one comes back short. Pages are numbered, so changing the size partway would shift them. `--limit 150` asks for 100 twice and keeps 150, like `gh cache list`.
- **The pull request check reuses `gh issue delete`'s lookup.** The [issue lookup](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/fc4b137cdef0a6bd28fd461b7cf9c84a5812a8cd/pkg/cmd/issue/shared/lookup.go#L136-L209) runs once, behind the client interface, so command tests use the mock.
- **Placement.** `artifact` sits under "Targeted commands" in `gh issue --help`, as `deploy-key` and `autolink` do under `gh repo`. It inherits `-R` from `gh issue`.
- **Unlimited by default.** `--limit` has no default in the help, and every artifact is listed. `--limit 0` is a flag error, "invalid limit: 0", like `gh issue list`.

This adds the `--attach` behavior for several documents from the `gh issue artifact create` design in #14525, ahead of the command itself.

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`--attach` uploads a local image or video. If the Markdown already references the file, gh replaces that reference with the uploaded URL. Otherwise it appends the file to the Markdown.

Today this works on one body at a time. `UploadAndAttach` takes one Markdown string and one set of files. `gh issue artifact create`, later in this stack, creates one artifact from each Markdown file, and `--attach` applies to all of them:

```
gh issue artifact create 142 signin-plan.md barista-notes.md --attach signin-flow.png
```

Calling `UploadAndAttach` once per file would upload `signin-flow.png` twice. It would also append the image to any file that doesn't reference it.

The new `UploadAndAttachDocuments` takes several documents and one set of files:

- It checks every document before the first upload. With several documents, a file that no document references is an error that names the file, and nothing is uploaded. There is no one body to append it to.
- It uploads each file once, in order, and stops at the first failure, like `UploadAndAttach`. Every document that references a file gets that file's URL.
- Each document resolves its references against its own directory first and the working directory second, the rule from the previous pull request in this stack.
- Each document gets its own result: its Markdown, which of its files uploaded, and the upload error if one of its files failed or was never tried. `create` will use this to decide whether to save each artifact.

With one document, it behaves exactly like `UploadAndAttach`, including appending unreferenced files. No command calls it with several documents until `gh issue artifact create`.

<!--

`UploadAndAttach` now runs through the new code, as its one-document case:

```go
// One document owns every file, so what it doesn't reference is appended
results, err := u.UploadAndAttachDocuments(ctx, []Document{{Markdown: md, Dir: markdownDir}}, assets)
if len(results) == 0 {
	// Refused before any upload, with md unchanged
	return md, UploadResult{}, err
}
```

- One path keeps the upload order, the failure contract and the append rule from drifting apart. The six existing `--attach` commands and their tests don't change.
- A document's attachments are the files it references, or every file when it is the only document. Each document fills in URLs only for its own attachments. A file a document references in a place gh can't rewrite, such as a reference definition continued onto the next line of a blockquote, is appended to that document, as `UploadAndAttach` already does. That way no upload is left unlinked.
- An unreferenced file is reported as `*UnreferencedError`, with every such path as typed, in attach order. Its own message is `no document references ./latte-art.png`, and `create` can reword it the way #14525 shows. With no documents at all, every file is refused the same way.
- A document's `Err` is the error that stopped the uploads, whenever it left one of that document's files without a URL. A document whose files all uploaded has no error, even if a later file fails. A caller saves a document when its `Err` is nil or its `Uploaded` isn't empty. `create` will save each artifact by that rule.
- `Uploaded` lists the document's files rather than counting them, so a caller can name what reached the server. `UploadResult` keeps its count for the existing commands.

This applies the reference rule from the `gh issue artifact create` design in #14525 to the six commands that already have `--attach`.

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`--attach` uploads a local image or video. If the body already references the file, gh replaces that reference with the uploaded URL. Otherwise it appends the file to the body.

To match a reference to an attached file, gh compares absolute paths. Until now, every reference resolved against the working directory. That breaks a common layout: a Markdown file kept beside its images.

```
docs/plan.md           contains ![Sign-in flow](./signin-flow.png)
docs/signin-flow.png
```

Running `gh issue create --body-file docs/plan.md --attach docs/signin-flow.png` from the project root looked for `./signin-flow.png` in the root. Nothing matched, so gh left the local path in the body and appended the image at the end.

A reference in a `--body-file` now resolves against that file's directory first. If that matches no attachment, it falls back to the working directory, so references that matched before still match. `--body` and standard input have no file, so they resolve against the working directory as before.

The rule lives in the shared `--attach` code, so `gh issue create`, `gh issue edit`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr create`, `gh pr edit` and `gh pr comment` all follow it. Each command's help gains one sentence: "Paths in a `--body-file` are relative to its directory, falling back to the working directory." The [`gh` agent skill](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/2f195d6788434d355990f3439d22da009040be17/skills/gh/SKILL.md) in this repository describes the same rule.

### Key points

Each way of reading a reference (as written, unescaped, percent-decoded) is tried beside the body file first, then in the working directory:

```go
spellings := candidatePaths(dest)
paths := make([]string, 0, 2*len(spellings))
if markdownDir != "" {
	for _, s := range spellings {
		// Rooted and drive-relative Windows paths are never moved into the folder
		if isRelativePath(s) {
			paths = append(paths, filepath.Join(markdownDir, s))
		}
	}
}
// The working directory comes second, so earlier matches still work
paths = append(paths, spellings...)
```

- The file beside the body file wins. If `signin-flow.png` and `docs/signin-flow.png` are both attached, `./signin-flow.png` in `docs/plan.md` now takes the one in `docs/` and the other is appended. Before, it took the one in the working directory. This only matters when a reference could name an attached file in either place.
- A reference that now matches follows the existing rules for matched references. So a video written as a reference-style image beside the body file is now refused before anything uploads, and the command exits 1. Before, that reference matched nothing, so gh appended the video, left the local path in the body and exited 0.
- The directory is a required parameter of `UploadAndAttach`, not an optional setting. Every caller has to say where its Markdown came from, and `""` means it came from no file. A new `--attach` command can't forget it.
- `--body-file -` sets no directory, since standard input has no folder:

  ```go
  opts.Body = string(b)
  // Standard input keeps the working directory
  if bodyFile != "-" {
  	opts.BodyDir = filepath.Dir(bodyFile)
  }
  ```

- Only `--body-file` sets a directory. A template's folder is never used, because template text is a starting point the user edits.
- The directory is the one in the path as typed. A symlinked body file resolves beside the link, not its target.

body:
This is a "map" issue for the PR stack listed below. It should be closed when the final PR in the stack is merged.

This stack adds `gh issue artifact`, a command group in preview for the Markdown documents and links attached to an issue. It has six commands: `list`, `view`, `create`, `edit`, `delete` and `download`. The stack also changes `--attach` in two ways that `create` needs, documents the commands in the `gh` agent skill, and lets `edit` restore an earlier version.

```bash
gh issue artifact create 142 signin-plan.md --attach ./signin-flow.png
```

The design is in #14529, with one issue per command: #14523 (`list`), #14524 (`view`), #14525 (`create`), #14526 (`edit`), #14527 (`delete`) and #14528 (`download`). Each design issue has a screen for every scenario.

### The stack 🥞

Ten pull requests, listed in reading order from the bottom. Each is based on the one below it. The total is about 3,100 lines of production code, a 440-line generated mock, 9,500 lines of tests and 100 lines of docs across 49 files, so most of the bulk is tests. Each code pull request has a video of the built `gh` in [bagtoad/issue-artifacts-demo](https://github.com/bagtoad/issue-artifacts-demo).

| # | PR | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #14564 | `--attach` resolves references in a `--body-file` against the file's own directory |
| 2 | #14565 | `--attach` uploads one set of files for several Markdown documents |
| 3 | #14566 | The command group, its API client and shared package, and `list` |
| 4 | #14567 | `view` |
| 5 | #14568 | `delete`, and the result lines the later commands share |
| 6 | #14569 | `download` |
| 7 | #14570 | `create` |
| 8 | #14571 | `edit` |
| 9 | #14572 | The `gh issue artifact` section in the `gh` agent skill |
| 10 | #14580 | `edit --restore-version`, which restores an earlier version |
| 11 | Pending | Artifact URLs: the `url` field, URL arguments, and `--web` on documents. It waits for the API to return artifact URLs. |

### How to read it

**Numbers 1 and 2 change `--attach`.** Number 1 is the only one that changes existing commands: the six `--attach` commands now resolve references in a `--body-file` against its directory first. Number 2 is groundwork for `create`, and no command reaches it until number 7.

**Start the command group at 3.** It sets up the client, the shared package and the command group that every later number uses. `list` is the simplest command.

**Numbers 4 to 8 add one command each,** and each reuses number 3's packages. Number 5 adds the result lines that `download`, `create` and `edit` also print.

**Number 6 holds the file safety rules, and number 7 is the largest.**

**Number 9 is documentation only.** It documents the six commands in the `gh` agent skill, as #14261 did for `--attach`.

**Number 10 adds `--restore-version` to `edit`.** It saves an earlier version's name and content as a new version, and documents the flag in the `gh` agent skill.

**Each diff shows only its own layer,** because each pull request is based on the one below it. There is nothing to filter out.

**The stack merges bottom to top.**

title: gh pr close <URL> --delete-branch can force-delete a same-named branch in an unrelated repository

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: priority-3
labels.description: Affects a small number of users or is largely cosmetic

labels.name: gh-pr
labels.description: relating to the gh pr command

body:
### Describe the bug

Running `gh pr close <PR URL> --delete-branch` from an unrelated local repository can force-delete a local branch in that repository if it has the same name as the PR's head branch. The command closes the selected PR, then looks up the branch by name in the current working directory and runs `git branch -D` there. An unpushed commit on the unrelated branch loses its branch reference.

This is related to #14537, which reports the same class of problem in `gh pr merge`. `gh pr close` has a separate cleanup path in `pkg/cmd/pr/close/close.go`; fixing `pr merge` alone does not change it.

### Affected version

Local build of `cli/cli` trunk at `9b031151a825bda919203c5202876a725d637368`:

```
gh version 9b03115 (2026-09-29)
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Have an open PR in `owner-a/repo-a` with head branch `feature-x`.
2. In an unrelated local repository `owner-b/repo-b`, have a local branch also named `feature-x` with an unpushed commit. Keep another branch checked out, and run the command from this repository.
3. Run `gh pr close https://github.com/owner-a/repo-a/pull/123 --delete-branch` (substitute the actual PR number).

I confirmed this command path with mocked GraphQL, REST, and Git interactions, without closing a live PR. The URL selector leaves `DeleteLocalBranch` enabled, and the Git stub for `git branch -D feature-x` is consumed.

### Expected vs actual behavior

Expected: Closing a PR in repo A must not delete a branch in unrelated repo B, even if the names match. If local cleanup cannot establish that the branch belongs to the selected PR, it should skip that cleanup.

Actual: `gh pr close` checks only whether `feature-x` exists in the current directory's Git repository, then runs `git branch -D feature-x`. Git's merged-branch safety check is bypassed, so unpushed local commits can lose their branch reference.

### Logs

The isolated mocked reproduction passed:

```
=== RUN   TestIssueReproURLDeletesSameNamedLocalBranch
--- PASS: TestIssueReproURLDeletesSameNamedLocalBranch (0.00s)
PASS
```

The relevant paths are [`DeleteLocalBranch = !cmd.Flags().Changed("repo")`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/9b031151a825bda919203c5202876a725d637368/pkg/cmd/pr/close/close.go#L50), the [name-only local branch lookup and deletion](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/9b031151a825bda919203c5202876a725d637368/pkg/cmd/pr/close/close.go#L113-L138), and [`git branch -D`](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/9b031151a825bda919203c5202876a725d637368/git/client.go#L668-L677).

title: `gh pr merge <url> --delete-branch` removes a worktree and deletes a same-named branch in the cwd's unrelated repository

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: priority-3
labels.description: Affects a small number of users or is largely cosmetic

labels.name: gh-pr
labels.description: relating to the gh pr command

body:
### Describe the bug

`gh pr merge <PR-URL> --delete-branch` runs its local cleanup in the repository of the **current working directory**, even when that repository is not the one the PR belongs to. It matches the head branch by **name only**. If a linked worktree there has a branch with the same name checked out, gh removes that worktree and force-deletes the branch. The branch and worktree belong to an unrelated repository.

`git worktree remove` (without `--force`) only refuses uncommitted changes, so a clean worktree whose branch holds **unpushed commits** is removed. `git branch -D` then leaves those commits reachable only from the reflog, so the work is effectively lost.

Version: `gh version 2.100.0 (2026-09-03)`, macOS.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Repo A (`owner-a/repo-a`) has an open PR whose head branch is `feature-x`.
2. An unrelated local repo B, whose remote is a different GitHub repository, has a linked worktree with its own branch also named `feature-x`. That branch holds a commit that has not been pushed.
3. With the cwd anywhere inside repo B, run:
   `gh pr merge https://github.com/owner-a/repo-a/pull/N --merge --delete-branch`
4. The PR in repo A merges and its remote branch is deleted, as expected. **In addition**, gh removes repo B's worktree and deletes repo B's local `feature-x`. The unpushed commit is no longer reachable from any ref. A process running in that worktree (a build, in our case) was also broken.

### Where it comes from (v2.100.0 source)

- `pkg/cmd/pr/merge/merge.go:124`: `opts.CanDeleteLocalBranch = !cmd.Flags().Changed("repo")`. A URL selector does not set `--repo`, so local cleanup stays enabled.
- `merge.go:594`: `localBranchExists: opts.CanDeleteLocalBranch && opts.GitClient.HasLocalBranch(ctx, pr.HeadRefName)`. This is evaluated in the cwd's repo, by name, and nothing checks that the cwd's repo is the PR's repository.
- `merge.go:494-504`: if the branch is checked out in another linked worktree, gh calls `WorktreeRemove` and then `DeleteLocalBranch` (`git branch -D`). This worktree handling appears to have come in with #13380.

Passing `--repo` avoids it, because `CanDeleteLocalBranch` becomes false, and the remote branch is still deleted.

### Expected behavior

Local cleanup should only touch a repository whose remote actually is the PR's base (or head) repository. For example, skip local cleanup unless one of the cwd repo's remotes resolves to the PR's repo, and/or unless the local branch's upstream tracks the PR's head repo and branch.

Independently, gh should not remove a worktree, or force-delete a branch, whose tip has commits that are not on the PR head (the merged commit). A safe check is that the local tip is equal to, or an ancestor of, `headRefOid`; otherwise, skip and warn. `git branch -D` bypasses git's own merged check, so this is the only guard.

### Additional context

This mostly bites people who work across several repos with a shared branch-naming convention (e.g. tooling that names branches `claude/<topic>`), or who merge a PR by URL from whichever repo their shell happens to be in. Nothing in the output hints that a different repository was touched: gh prints `Removed worktree <path>` and `Deleted local branch <name>`, and the path belongs to the other repo.

body:
This is the design for `gh issue artifact`, a new command group for working with issue artifacts from the terminal. Issue artifacts are Markdown documents and links attached to an issue. They aren't GitHub Actions artifacts, which `gh run download` handles.

Each subcommand has its own design issue, with its help text and the expected output for every scenario:

| Command | What it does | Design |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gh issue artifact list` | List the artifacts on an issue | #14523 |
| `gh issue artifact view` | Show an artifact, or open a link in the browser | #14524 |
| `gh issue artifact create` | Create artifacts from files, URLs or text | #14525 |
| `gh issue artifact edit` | Rename an artifact, replace its content or restore an earlier version | #14526 |
| `gh issue artifact delete` | Delete artifacts | #14527 |
| `gh issue artifact download` | Save artifacts as files | #14528 |

The screenshots in those issues are mockups

## Shared behavior

These apply to every subcommand:

- An artifact is addressed by its issue and its number on that issue, as in `gh issue artifact view 142 2`, or by its URL. Names don't have to be unique, so gh never looks an artifact up by name.
- The issue argument takes a number or a URL, like other `gh issue` commands. Pull requests aren't supported.
- GitHub Enterprise Server isn't supported.
- Documents are `generic` or `plan` artifacts, and links are `link` artifacts. On disk, a link is an Internet Shortcut (`.url`) file, which opens in the browser on Windows and macOS.
- `list` and `view` support `--json`, `--jq` and `--template`, with every field the API returns.
- When piped, `create`, `edit`, `delete` and `download` print one tab-separated line per artifact: status, number, name or path, source, and the reason for a failure or skip. Any failure exits 1.
- `--attach` uploads images and videos that a document references, like `gh issue create --attach`.
- Existing `gh issue` commands don't show or export artifacts. Every `--attach` command, `gh pr` included, now resolves references in a `--body-file` against the file's own directory first, then the working directory.

--- ## `gh issue artifact edit`
What is changing - **Content**: Replace an artifact's body with a file's contents - **Links**: Update a link artifact from a `.url` file - **Attachments**: `--attach` also works when editing, and appends unreferenced attachments - **Content**: Rename an artifact with `--name`, keeping its body - **Content**: An artifact URL can replace the issue and number - **Content**: Replace an artifact's body from standard input - **Attachments**: `--attach` on its own appends to the artifact's current body - **Errors**: Editing needs at least one of `--name`, `--body`, `--body-file`, `--attach` or `--restore-version` - **Links**: Update a link artifact's URL with `--body` - **Errors**: A link only takes an http(s) URL, from any source, or a `.url` file, so a text file is rejected - **Errors**: A `.url` file can only update a link - **Errors**: `--attach` can't be used with a link, because a link has no Markdown body - **Errors**: `--body` and `--body-file` are mutually exclusive - **Scripting**: When piped, edit prints one `\t\t\t\t` line, like `create` and `delete` - **Versions**: `--restore-version` saves an earlier version's name and body as a new version - **Versions**: When the current name and body already match the version, nothing is saved - **Errors**: A version the API didn't return fails before anything is saved - **Errors**: `--restore-version` must be at least 1 - **Errors**: `--restore-version` can't be combined with `--name`, `--body`, `--body-file` or `--attach` - **Scripting**: When piped, a restore prints one `restored` line - **Scripting**: When piped, a restore with nothing to restore prints a `skipped` line with the reason

#### `create` *Input:* ```bash $ gh issue artifact create --help ``` *Output:* ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7864292-4d1f-441a-b7d2-531bda70c7c1)

--- ## `gh issue artifact create`
What is changing - **Files**: Create an artifact from a file, named after the file - **Files**: Name an artifact with the text after `#`, parsed like `--attach` alt text - **Files**: A `#` inside a file name works, because the longest existing path wins - **Files**: Characters an artifact name can't contain are removed from names taken from file names - **Files**: Create one artifact per file - **No file**: Create an artifact from standard input, which requires `--name` - **No file**: Create an artifact from inline text - **Files**: `--type plan` saves a document as a plan; files still default to `generic` - **Links**: A URL argument creates a link artifact, named by `--name` - **Links**: A URL without `--name` is named after its host - **Links**: A `.url` Internet Shortcut file creates a link artifact - **Attachments**: Upload images with `--attach`, rewrite references to them, and append the rest - **Attachments**: A file's Markdown references resolve against that file's directory - **Attachments**: A reference that matches nothing next to its file falls back to the working directory - **Attachments**: With several files, each attachment replaces its references in whichever files use it - **Errors**: With several files, an attachment no file references is an error, and nothing is uploaded or created - **Scripting**: When piped, each artifact gets a `\t\t\t\t` line on stdout, in argument order - **Scripting**: When piped, failures are also lines on stdout, with an empty number and a reason, and the command exits 1 - **Errors**: Content without a file name needs `--name` - **Errors**: With no file, URL, `--body` or `--body-file`, create fails with a usage error and never reads stdin implicitly - **Errors**: `--name` only applies when creating one artifact - **Errors**: Files cannot be combined with `--body` or `--body-file` - **Errors**: `--type` only applies to documents, since links come from URLs and `.url` files - **Errors**: A `.url` file without a usable URL is rejected before anything is created - **Errors**: Binary files are rejected before anything is created, like `gh gist create` - **Errors**: An empty or whitespace-only file is rejected before anything is created, like `gh gist create` - **Errors**: Size limits are the server's; an oversized file fails on its own line while the others are created - **Errors**: Without permission to write artifacts, the API's 404 message is the reason - **Files**: A symlinked file is read like any other file, and named by the path as typed

--- ## `gh issue artifact view`
What is changing - **Terminal**: View an artifact like `gh issue view`, with its body rendered as Markdown and its edit history - **Terminal**: A link shows its URL where the body would be - **Terminal**: An artifact URL can replace the issue and number - **Versions**: `--version` shows an earlier version, marked `Viewing` in the edit history - **Scripting**: When piped, view prints `key:` lines in a fixed order, `--`, then the body - **Scripting**: When piped with `--version`, the name, version, editor and body come from that version - **Browser**: `--web` opens a link artifact's URL in the browser - **Browser**: `--web` opens a document's page on GitHub - **JSON output**: `view` takes the same `--json` fields as `list`, plus `versions` - **JSON output**: `--json versions` has every version the API returns, including each version's body - **Errors**: A missing artifact number shows the API's 404, as returned - **Errors**: A version the API didn't return fails - **Errors**: `--version` must be at least 1 - **Errors**: `--version` can't be combined with `--json` or `--web`

--- ## `gh issue artifact list`
What is changing - **Terminal**: List every artifact on an issue as a table, in number order, with a header - **Terminal**: The issue argument can be a URL, which also names the repository - **Terminal**: `-R` selects the repository, like other gh commands - **Terminal**: `--limit` stops after N artifacts; the header still shows the total - **Scripting**: When piped, the same columns are tab-separated, with exact timestamps and no header row - **Terminal**: An issue with no artifacts prints a message to stderr in a terminal, and exits 0 - **Filtering**: When a filter matches nothing, the message says so, and the command exits 0 - **Filtering**: `--type` lists only artifacts of one type, filtered on the server - **Filtering**: `--type generic` also returns plans, which keep their `plan` type - **Filtering**: `--type plan` lists the same documents as `--type generic`, plans and generic artifacts alike - **Errors**: An unknown `--type` value lists the accepted values - **Errors**: `--limit` must be at least 1 - **Errors**: Pull requests are rejected, whether given as a number or a URL - **Errors**: A host without artifact storage fails with the API's 503, as returned - **Errors**: GitHub Enterprise Server is refused before any request - **JSON output**: `--json` selects fields, with keys sorted like every gh `--json` command
